OMP-545-s02: summarize reads that JSONL file and writes JSON plus a markdown table, one row per (experiment, arm, model), sorted by that key, plus pooled totals. A repetition is (task_id, repetition). First outcome is the attempt 1 record (pass 1, fail 0, missing or any other status null). Final outcome is the highest attempt whose status is pass or fail; a later harness_defect or invalid_evidence does not decide. ac_success is final passes over decidable finals, with a Wilson 95% score interval (z = 1.959964, proportion capped to [0,1]). first_pass_rate is that ratio for first outcomes. A task passes one side when every decidable repetition on that side is 1, and the task rate is passing tasks over counted tasks. Record status counts cover every record. undecided is repetitions whose final outcome is null. Sums of tokens, cost_usd (Decimal string), turns, interventions, and latency skip null-token records; unknown counts those records. cost_per_success and success_per_minute are null when the summed input tokens are null, and each is null when its own divisor is 0 or unknown. A repeated (experiment, arm, model, task_id, repetition, attempt) exits 1 and writes no output. DEFAULT_OPERATIONS names project.list/context/status/decisions, mission.status, stop.status, mission.pause, and stop.engage. load_ingress_config(path) reads a JSON object with workspace_id (UUID) and an optional operations list (default DEFAULT_OPERATIONS) and raises ValueError for a missing or invalid workspace id, a name the client contract does not declare, or an empty list. create_ingress_app(config, upstream, transport) returns an ASGI app that forwards only an allowed operation's method and exact path, with {workspace_id} equal to the configured UUID and every other path parameter matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}, carrying only the Authorization, X-OMP-Contract-SHA256, Content-Type, and Accept headers, and relays the upstream status, body, and content type. Any other request, any query string, or any '..' segment is 404 not_found; a body over 64 KiB is 413; an unreachable upstream is 502; every refusal carries X-OMP-Ingress: refused and makes no upstream call. One stderr line per request names the method, path, operation (or -), a 12-hex sha256 of the bearer (or -), and the status. add_parser/run provide omp-work ingress serve --config PATH [--port 54323] [--upstream http://127.0.0.1:54322] and bind 127.0.0.1. Operations outside the config and every extra must get 404 with X-OMP-Ingress: refused. OMP-431-s03 pinned egress fetch and push, using the s01 address and destination rules. Resolver(host, port) returns addresses; Connector(ip, port, timeout) returns a socket. open_pinned resolves at call time with no cache: a blocked IP literal raises EgressRefused with the blocked_address code and calls neither the resolver nor the connector; an empty answer is invalid; any blocked answer raises EgressRefused with that code and the offending ip and does not connect; a public IP literal must resolve only to itself or the answer is invalid; otherwise the connector is called with the first address, that port, and the timeout (default 30s). tls wraps the socket with the default SSL context (CERT_REQUIRED, check_hostname, optional ca_bundle) and SNI equal to the host. ResearchFetchService.fetch records every call on channel fetch with the request url and the identity mission, worker, workspace, project, and stage. A non-http(s) URL is scheme_not_allowed and a missing host is invalid, both before any lookup or send. A research_refusal hit raises EgressRefused with that s01 code (method_not_allowed, request_body, auth_header, url_credentials, query_credential) and sends nothing. A clean http(s) GET or HEAD is vetted, then open_pinned looks the name up again and connects to the connect-time address; the vet lookup is not reused, so a public address at vet and a blocked address at connect is refused and the connector is not called. One request is issued with the caller headers only (no Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization is added), redirects are not followed, and no cookie jar is kept. Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie2 are dropped. Statuses such as 302 and 401 are returned as FetchResult(status, headers, body). A certificate failure is recorded as tls_error and re-raised; another exchange failure is recorded as exchange_failed. check_push_destination requires https (else scheme_not_allowed), a host, no userinfo (else url_credentials), and no blocked IP literal (else the blocked_address code). The origin must be granted by an unexpired network_access destination under the s01 rule: exact scheme, normalized host, and port; accepted forms are https://h[:p], http://h[:p], h:p as https, h as https port 443, and bracketed [v6] or [v6]:port; a path other than empty or /, a query, a fragment, userinfo, or another scheme grants nothing; expires_at <= now is expired and a naive expiry is UTC; the caller now is used, not the wall clock; a non-network_access policy does not grant. Otherwise destination_not_allowed. The granting policy id is returned. deliver_push runs that check again, POSTs once through open_pinned with TLS, drops Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie2, and records channel push (klass standing and the policy id when the origin was granted; klass none when the check itself refuses).

OMP-431-s04: asyncio default-deny egress HTTP proxy. One unix socket per sandbox identity at <dir>/proxy.sock (mode 0600), created by open_sandbox(identity, dir) and removed by close_sandbox(identity); the identity is the sandbox binding and is never read from a request (an X-OMP-Mission header is ignored). One request per client connection; the policy is read fresh from policy_source(identity, now) for each request; every client response carries Connection: close and the connection then closes, so pipelined bytes are dropped. Plain absolute-form requests: a refusal is 403 with JSON {"code": code} and one EgressRecord; a research identity is delegated to the s03 fetch service (channel fetch, the service's own record) for both allow and refusal; a model destination is forwarded to model_proxy_upstream; an allowed registry, remote, or standing destination is dialed by resolver(host) and connector(ip, port, timeout) and sent origin-form with Connection: close; the upstream response is relayed and recorded (channel http) with the effective host, port, ip, url, klass, and policy_id. A registry is stored as https and decide never matches it for an http request, so an http absolute-form request whose destination the policy also defines as an https origin is re-judged as that https origin while a genuinely unnamed destination still refuses destination_not_allowed. CONNECT host:port is judged as an https tunnel: model destinations and standing destinations whose host is not a project remote are tunnelled (200 Connection Established) and recorded (channel connect); a standing destination whose host is a project remote is inspected instead of opened as an opaque tunnel, so the inner request is decided (tls unset records klass standing, code tls_inspection_required, and does not dial); registry, remote, and research destinations need TLS inspection and are refused tls_inspection_required when tls is unset; anything else gets decide's code (destination_not_allowed, including an IP literal); with tls set to a GatewayCA the gateway replies 200, upgrades the client connection to a CA-signed leaf for the tunnel authority, reads exactly one inner request, and re-runs the plain-http path for it as https with tunnel False against the tunnel authority (the inner request's own host and scheme are ignored, so a relative or absolute target is judged as https against the authority); a leaf that cannot be minted, an empty inner read, an unverifiable upstream certificate (recorded tls_error), and an upstream dial failure (recorded upstream_failed) all end the request with no inner request reaching the upstream; the same one-request Connection: close rule and the same verdicts apply, the upstream leg is TLS with SNI equal to the host verified against system trust or upstream_ca_bundle, and research still goes to the s03 fetch service as an https URL. Every record names the bound identity's workspace, project, mission, worker, and stage.

OMP-431 egress address policy: blocked_address refuses an egress target with invalid (unparseable), metadata (169.254.169.254, 168.63.129.16, 100.100.100.200, fd00:ec2::254), nat64_u_octet (RFC 6052 64:ff9b:1::/48 with a non-zero u-octet), or not_global (not globally routable, or multicast), and returns None only for a globally routable unicast address; IPv6 transition formats are unwrapped to the embedded IPv4 first: IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible ::/96 (except :: and ::1), 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo client, and NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 and 64:ff9b:1::/48; Identity frozen dataclass; research_refusal refusing non-GET/HEAD, request bodies, auth headers, URL credentials, and query credentials; EgressRecord frozen dataclass; EgressRecorder protocol and MemoryRecorder; build_policy (the only EgressPolicy constructor, no worktree input) normalizes a host by lower-casing, dropping a trailing dot, stripping brackets, and canonicalizing an IP literal, requires model_proxy ("host:port" or "[v6]:port", explicit port) or raises ValueError, keeps a registry only as https://host[:port] (default 443; OMP-431-s01-s05: Request frozen dataclass (scheme, host, port, method, path, query, headers, has_body, tunnel) and Verdict frozen dataclass (allowed, klass model|registry|remote|standing|research|none, code, policy_id); decide(policy, identity, req, now) normalizes the host, defaults a missing port to 443 (https) or 80 (http), treats tunnel as method CONNECT, and applies in order: (1) (host,port) equal policy.model_proxy -> allowed model; (2) research stage -> refused research with the research_refusal code, else allowed research; (3) a standing destination grants the request's exact scheme, host, and port for any request path or query (forms https://h[:p], http://h[:p], h:p as https, h as https:443, and bracketed [v6] or [v6]:port as https; a destination whose path is not "/" or empty, or that carries a query, fragment, userinfo, or another scheme, grants nothing, as does a policy expired at now; an IP literal matches only itself) -> allowed standing with policy_id=str(policy.policy_id); (4) registry: https and (host,port) in policy.registries -> tunnel or non-GET/HEAD is method_not_allowed, body is request_body, else allowed with policy_id=policy.decision_id; OMP-431-s01-s06: (5) remote (repository stage): matches (scheme, host, port, repo) when scheme, normalized host, and default-filled port match and its repeatedly percent-decoded safe path (empty, ".", ".." segments or backslash drop match) equals repo or lies under it by whole segment with optional ".git" (/o/r, /o/r.git, /o/r/..., /o/r.git/...; not /o/rx); read-only rule in order: query service=git-receive-pack (any case) or path ending /git-receive-pack -> refused remote, git_receive_pack; POST allowed only when path is exactly <repo>/git-upload-pack or <repo>.git/git-upload-pack, otherwise method_not_allowed; tunnel or method other than GET/HEAD -> method_not_allowed; GET/HEAD with body -> request_body; else allowed remote with policy_id=policy.decision_id; (6) otherwise refused, klass none, destination_not_allowed; a refusal raised after a match keeps that match's klass OMP-403-s06: a non-research identity whose request a standing network_access destination would allow is still refused klass standing: git-receive-pack on any host (query service=git-receive-pack or a path ending /git-receive-pack, including after percent-decoding) with code git_receive_pack, and a non-GET/HEAD, tunneled, or bodied request to a project remote host with code control_plane_action; both keep the standing policy id. GET/HEAD without a body to that host, and a non-receive-pack request to a standing host that is not a project remote, stay allowed standing. Research returns before this rule.

OMP-431-s08-s02 research filesystem jail, started as unshare --mount --pid --fork python -m omp_work.egress_research_jail. A research root reads ca_cert_path before any mount and exits nonzero without writing a certificate when the path is missing, unreadable, or empty. Makes / rprivate, mounts a tmpfs as the new root, read-only rbinds /usr, and recreates /bin, /lib, /lib64, and /sbin as the host symlink or a read-only rbind. Writes /etc/passwd and /etc/group from the host, the shared s06 resolver texts, and the CA bytes at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt. Bind-mounts /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random, and /dev/urandom. Mounts a fresh procfs, or on EPERM or EACCES leaves /proc empty and never bind-mounts the host /proc. /tmp is mode 1777 and a research root creates /home/research. pivot_root(new, new/.old), chdir /home/research for a research root, creates setup_ok through the old root, umount2 /.old with MNT_DETACH, removes /.old, and stays PID 1. It forks and execve's setpriv --bounding-set=-all --inh-caps=-all --no-new-privs plus the config argv with the worker environment in the child, then exits with the child's status. A signal death exits 128 plus the signal number, because PID 1 ignores SIGKILL sent from inside the namespace. Does not call chroot. Imports happen at module load, before the pivot. Codacy: the jail root, /home, and /home/research chmod 0755 and /tmp chmod 1777 are the intended POSIX modes for a tmpfs root the unprivileged worker must traverse, and the setpriv execve is a fixed argv list with no shell and no user-controlled executable, so the Bandit B103/B606 and insecure-file-permissions/dangerous-os-exec findings are suppressed with nosec/nosemgrep. OMP-417: root "worker" returns before the CA read. It builds the same tmpfs jail without a CA file and without /home/research, bind-mounts the config worktree read-write at /work by default, and bind-mounts each absolute ro_binds file read-only at the caller's path. With worktree_readonly, validates every ro_dirs entry and non-None audit_dir as an absolute non-root string before any mount, recursively binds the worktree read-only at /work, binds ro_dirs read-only in ascending path depth, then overlays audit_dir read-write at /work/.omp when set. Both directory binders accept pre-existing targets, so nested directory binds and a real worktree .omp can be overlaid. The read-only remount keeps the source mount's nosuid, nodev, noexec, nosymfollow, atime, and relatime flags so a user namespace accepts it. A recursive read-only rbind keeps those flags on the bound mount and remounts each submount read-only with that submount's own flags, so a nosuid or nodev source does not return EPERM and a child mount is not left read-write. pivot_root then chdirs to /work. OMP-431-s06/s07: egress sandbox runner. Executes the worker in isolated user, mount, network, and PID namespaces with an AF_UNIX record.sock (mode 0700) listener that records refused raw egress attempts as EgressRecord entries on channel raw with code raw_egress_refused; unshare, setpriv, and ip must be on PATH and run by absolute path, the worker command is the caller argv with no shell, and a recorder failure is ignored. run_sandboxed also takes gateway=None, workservice (host, port)|None, and ca_cert_path=None: with a gateway it calls gateway.open_sandbox(identity, dir) (closing it afterward) and binds <dir>/dns.sock (chmod 0600), answering A/AAAA from the gateway resolver only for the model proxy host, a named registry or remote host, or an unexpired standing host the gateway policy_source(identity, now) grants, refusing every other name with code name_not_allowed recorded on channel dns and never forwarding it; with workservice it binds <dir>/ws.sock (chmod 0600), a relay that connects only to that host and port; without a gateway or workservice neither socket exists and names fail as before. enqueue_job and claim_job run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Enqueue requires resources cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls as integers >= 0, capabilities stored sorted and unique, lease_seconds 1..3600, a work item and parent in the workspace, and, when trial_id is set, a proposed trial of that work on an admitted or running campaign. A cancelled parent or ancestor raises job_cancelled and writes no row. An identical job_id replays; any other row with that id is idempotency_conflict. The insert is source native, backlog, fence 0, plus an enqueued event. OMP-404-s05 adds an item-budget gate after the validations and before the insert, for the root item (the parent's chain top, or the work item itself): an exhausted usd/tokens/wall_clock dimension cancels the item tree and refuses, and a child that would take the tree past max_subagents cancels the tree and writes the subagents budget.exceeded alert first. A refusal returns {status refused, code budget_exceeded} from apply, and because a raise inside the transaction would roll back the alert and the stop, without a caller cursor enqueue_job raises JobError budget_exceeded only after the transaction commits (replays included). After a child insert the same transaction calls check_item_budget, so a child that crosses a subagents threshold writes the 50 or 80 row at enqueue. claim_job reads only the workers row, locks it, and with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED considers the oldest backlog native job whose capabilities the worker holds, whose resource weight (sum of the four fields) fits capacity minus the weight of that worker's unreleased reservations, that fits caller-specified resource_limits (cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls >= 0) against unreleased reservations plus the candidate job, and that has no cancelled ancestor; an invisible parent leaves the candidate unclaimable without halting later backlog scans; a candidate whose root item budget is exhausted returns job null instead of being leased. A trial job is leased only while the trial is proposed, the campaign is admitted or running, and the worker component is in compatibility.workers. The lease sets admitted, fence+1, attempt+1, worker_id, lease_expires_at, reservation {job_id}:{fence}, and a claimed event. An unknown or inactive worker is job_worker_unavailable; no match returns job null. OMP-430-s06: claim_job, as the first statement inside its transaction and before it locks the worker row, returns {status applied, job null} when the workspace's agent stop is engaged, so no job is leased (and no fence is spent) while stopped; the owner's release lets the next claim resume the same backlog job OMP-417-s05: after the worker is confirmed active and before the backlog scan, claim_job returns the oldest admitted job already leased to that worker which has a lease_resumed event not yet followed by a later resume_claimed; it appends resume_claimed with payload worker_id and fence and does not change the worker, fence, or reservation. An unknown or inactive worker still raises job_worker_unavailable before that lookup, and a stop still returns job null before the worker is locked. OMP-590-s02: claim_job takes optional job_id. When it is omitted the job_claim request stays workspace_id, worker_id, and resource_limits, and backlog selection stays oldest-first. A non-None job_id is included in that request hash and limits both the resumed-lease lookup and the backlog read to that job before either query locks a row or appends an event, so the targeted read does not scan unrelated backlog. A missing, incompatible, or stopped target returns job null and does not lease or resume a different job. Stop, capability, capacity, resource limits, ancestry, budget, trial, campaign, and component-manifest gates still apply to the target. OMP-595-s01: enqueue_job accepts optional cur, reusing validation, admission, operation/job idempotency, events and budget gates on caller-owned workspace/actor transaction without opening, committing or rolling back a transaction; enlisted budget refusals raise with effects pending for caller commit/rollback, while omitted cur preserves committed budget refusals.

OMP-404-s05: when any dimension is exhausted, check_item_budget also calls cancel_item_tree with reason budget_exceeded in the same transaction, so the alerts and the item-tree stopping commit together. sweep_item_budgets visits the workspace's source=native work items that carry an intake_publication receipt and have a non-terminal job, each in its own transaction, and returns the work ids whose tree check_item_budget stopped (work-clock enforcement with no usage row). alert_subagents_exceeded writes the subagents budget.exceeded row at the cap; the enqueue refusal path calls it, since check_item_budget never reports subagents exhausted OMP-595-s07-s01: task_deadline(cur, workspace, job, controls) is the shared task deadline: exact oldest job-tree created_at plus the smaller of the published wall_clock_seconds and a positive-integer controls.wall_clock_seconds, None once elapsed, DEFAULT_TASK_SECONDS from now only when neither limit exists.

OMP-590-s01: load_definition reads a JSON campaign definition into CampaignDefinition. objective is a nonempty string and domain is a ResearchDomain. trials is a nonempty list of objects with harness, a nonempty path resolved against the definition file's directory; the harness bytes are cached at load and candidate_digest is the SHA-256 of those bytes, so a later edit does not change the prepared trial. criteria is a nonempty list of Criterion objects with metric (nonempty, at most 128 characters), op (gte, gt, lte, lt, or eq), and a finite numeric threshold. timeout_seconds is an optional positive integer and defaults to 60. Unknown keys, duplicate keys, booleans used as numbers, and non-finite values are rejected. score_metrics returns supported or refuted: a status other than completed, a missing metric, or a non-finite metric refutes; otherwise it compares with >=, >, <=, <, and ==. The first failing criterion refutes and the reason names the failed status, metric, or comparison. When every criterion passes, the reason names the passed criteria count. score_campaign returns supported only when every verdict is supported, and that reason names the trial count; otherwise it refutes at the first failure and names that trial's 1-based index. Integer thresholds and observations remain finite at arbitrary precision; only floats undergo finiteness checks, so values beyond float range load and score without overflow. OMP-605-s01-s01: PreparedTrial appends id=None, parent=None, cost=1 constructor defaults; loaded ids default to t000, t001, etc. ASCII ids match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}; duplicate/generated collisions and self, forward, or unknown parents are rejected. Absent/null parents are roots; costs are finite positive non-boolean numbers. CampaignDefinition.search defaults to None; explicit search objects resolve fixed/greedy policy, width=1, seed=0, first criterion metric, and omitted budget via math.fsum(costs). Width is a positive integer, seed a nonnegative integer, metric names a declared criterion, and budget is finite positive; booleans, unknown keys, and total overflow are rejected. Greedy maximizes its metric; cached bytes, digests, and legacy scoring remain unchanged. OMP-605-s01-s03: search_steps(definition) returns a fresh trial-ordered dict keyed by resolved trial id (constructor-default ids resolved by position) with parent_id, children in definition order, cost, candidate_digest, and unset metric/infra_error; repeated digests stay distinct nodes. definition_commitment(definition) is the omp_work.v1.canonical.sha256 of objective, domain, timeout_seconds, ordered criteria, resolved search config, and ordered trials (id, parent, cost, candidate_digest) including unopened ones; it excludes paths, observations, and selection state, and raises ValueError when search is absent.

Prepare campaign specs and compatibility manifests via replayable component registration and cached content-addressed harness copies. OMP-605-s01-s04: with an explicit search the prepared spec evaluation_protocol_sha256 is definition_commitment(definition), binding objective, domain, timeout, criteria, search config, and the trial pool; without search it stays sha256 of the criteria list. Registration, caching, compatibility, and resources are unchanged.

cancel_job runs through NativeJobStore.run_operation. It locks the target and every same-workspace descendant with a recursive CTE on parent_job_id, FOR UPDATE, ordered by job_id. Each native backlog or admitted job becomes cancelled with cancel_reason, cancelled_at, and updated_at; an admitted job also gains fence+1, loses worker_id, and has its open {job_id}:{fence} reservation released as cancelled, so the holder's renew and settle raise job_fence_stale. Sealed and failed jobs stay. One cancelled event is appended per job cancelled. The result is {status, job_ids}. A target already cancelled for the same reason replays and does not write the job, its events, or its reservation again; a different reason is idempotency_conflict. A missing target, or a sealed or failed target, is invalid_request and writes nothing. OMP-404-s05 adds cancel_item_tree, the item-scoped counterpart the budget stopper calls with the caller's open cursor: it validates the reason, locks the work item's own jobs plus every parent_job_id descendant (whichever work item), in job_id order FOR UPDATE, then cancels the native backlog and admitted rows through the same _cancel_rows rules. It is a sub-operation of the enclosing transaction, not run_operation, so it stamps the enclosing operation id and has no separate replay; sealed, failed, and already-cancelled jobs are left alone

renew_lease, settle_job, and reconcile_jobs run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Renew and settle hold only a native admitted job whose worker_id and fence match and whose lease_expires_at is still after now; otherwise job_fence_stale and nothing is written. renew_lease adds lease_seconds to the job lease and the unreleased {job_id}:{fence} reservation expiry. settle_job maps succeeded to sealed and failed to failed. Each receipt role is audit, release, or evaluator; its evidence must validate as an R02 evidence document of kind receipt, and its issuer must be a registered workspace component whose kind equals that role; otherwise invalid_request and nothing is written. Settlement {outcome, fence, worker_id, receipts} is written once with settled_at, the reservation is released as settled, and a settled event is appended. A terminal job replays a byte-identical settlement under a new operation id and keeps the stored receipts; any other settlement is job_fence_stale. With no stop to apply, reconcile_jobs returns each admitted native job with lease_expires_at at or before now to backlog with fence+1, null worker_id and lease_expires_at, releases that reservation as lease_expired, appends a lease_expired event, and returns {status, job_ids}; a second call returns no job ids. OMP-430-s06: renew_lease, as the first statement inside its transaction and before the lease UPDATE, refuses with agent_stop_engaged and writes nothing when the workspace's agent stop is engaged. OMP-417-s05: while that stop is engaged reconcile_jobs writes nothing for any job and returns no job ids, so a lease that outlives its expiry stays admitted with the same worker, fence, and lease_expires_at. After release, the first reconcile handles each native admitted job that was leased when the stop was engaged (worker_id set, lease_expires_at after the engage time, a current-fence claimed event at or before that time, and no lease_resumed yet for that fence and release event id): an active holder keeps the worker and fence, sets lease_expires_at and the unreleased reservation expiry to now plus lease_seconds, and appends one lease_resumed event whose payload is worker_id, fence, and release_event_id; a holder that is missing or not active goes back to backlog with fence+1, null worker and lease, the reservation released as lease_recovered, and a lease_recovered event carrying release_event_id. A lease that had already expired before the stop, or that expires after it was resumed, is reclaimed as lease_expired. A second reconcile does not write another lease_resumed for the same job, fence, and release event. OMP-595-s03: LeaseAuthority dataclass and current_authority shared read-only query for workspace/job/worker/fence yielding live expiry, lost authority, or frozen ownership using DB clock and bounded transaction reads. OMP-595-s06: require_live_holder(cur, workspace_id, job_id, worker_id, fence) locks the job row and returns the live LeaseAuthority inside the caller's transaction; a stop-frozen lease raises JobError agent_stop_engaged and any other loss raises job_fence_stale.

OMP-315-s04: managed-trial evaluation worker on the s02 substrate. dispatch_managed_trial enqueues the managed-trial:<trial_id> native compute job with the research.managed_trial capability only when the work item's mission (v1.missions.mission_for_work) is approved or running, of kind research.run, and requested that capability; anything else raises ManagedTrialRefused(mission_not_authorized) and enqueues no job. evaluate_candidate(backend, protocol, *, candidate_tar, candidate_digest, evaluator_script, confirmation, cancel, scratch_dir=None) is the database-free loop in a scratch dir: it materializes the candidate tar (hash-checked) and runs protocol.candidate_command with protocol.requires and timeout_seconds; a nonzero exit, a non-completed run, a missing declared output, an output whose ancestor escapes the candidate directory (a symlinked parent is refused rather than followed, so a candidate cannot point a declared name at a host file), or an output that is not a regular file is candidate_failed (a candidate timeout records candidate_timed_out); the evaluator receives the candidate-dir path, not the resolved target. Otherwise it writes the evaluator as ./evaluate (0755) and input.json {outputs: {rel: absolute path}, confirmation: path|null}, and runs protocol.evaluator_command with the outputs and confirmation read-only; an exit mismatch, an unreadable or absent score.json, a non-bool valid, a non-finite or non-numeric metric, or a metric-name set different from the protocol's is evaluator_failed; a second evaluator run on empty outputs that returns valid true is evaluator_failed with negative_control accepted; otherwise the evaluation is qualified with output_digest over {relative: bytes}. The candidate never receives the confirmation. run(worker, job) observes first, then reads the trial row, the evaluator component descriptor (kind evaluator), the protocol digest from the campaign spec, and the candidate/protocol/evaluator/confirmation bytes from content_dir/<sha256>, each hash-checked; a missing, mismatched, or malformed input settles failed with no receipts and records nothing. On success it registers the TrialReceipt.receipt_bytes as a legacy_autoresearch custody artifact (source_ref job:<job_id>), records the legacy observation at issuer_kind legacy_autoresearch/source_ref job:<job_id> with payload {receipt_sha256, verdict, metrics} and execution_status completed when qualified, timed_out on a candidate timeout, else crashed, and settles one evaluator receipt whose issuer is trial.evaluator_sha256 and whose content_digest is the receipt sha with trust trusted and outcome succeeded when qualified, else untrusted and failed. A cancel at any step returns failed with no receipts and records nothing; run also refuses to register or observe when the worker's cancel event is already set after the final backend run, so a cancel that lands after the last run still records nothing. observe rebuilds the settlement from the stored observation without re-running. factory adds content_dir, an optional backend (default LocalJailBackend), and scratch_dir to the research_trial options; python -m omp_work.jobs.managed_trial check dispatches one managed job and ticks one worker to settlement

deliver_outbox drains one workspace's committed or failed usage_ledger omp_jobs.outbox rows to the usage ledger file; OMP-404 adds the kind='usage_ledger' filter so budget_alert rows written by jobs.budget have no file-ledger effect and stay untouched. Rows are read in event_id order under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. A failed row is committed again first (apply_commit, revision+1). An event whose usage_id is already in the ledger closes without appending; otherwise the payload is appended with research_ledger.append_ledger_event and counted, and a raised append returns the row to failed via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=False) for retry. A present usage_id is acknowledged and closed via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=True) plus close. A crash between the append and the state update leaves the row committed, so the next call finds the usage_id and closes without appending: the external effect happens at most once. State changes reuse contracts/v1/recovery, adding no second state machine

OMP-400-s03/OMP-475-s01: ProbeHandler and factory for omp.probe jobs. probe_job_id returns probe-<uuid4> when sleep_seconds is 0, otherwise probe-sleep<ms>-<uuid4> with ms = round(sleep_seconds*1000), and raises ValueError when sleep_seconds is negative, NaN, or infinite. probe_sleep_seconds returns that encoded sleep in seconds, or None when the sleep part is absent or malformed. run() and observe() sleep the encoded seconds when present, otherwise the configured sleep_seconds (default 0), then return outcome succeeded with empty receipts

OMP-400-s03/OMP-475-s02: production runner for native jobs with advisory lock and SIGTERM handling (run_worker), component registration via WorkClient (register_component), and substrate health probe polling (check). check(path, work_id, count, timeout, lease, sleep) sizes its probe lease with probe_lease_seconds(timeout, lease): None derives max(1, min(30, int(timeout // 4))), an explicit lease must be an int (not bool) in 1..3600 and below timeout else ValueError, and every job id is built with probe_job_id(sleep) before any enqueue so bad input raises and writes nothing; jobs are enqueued with that lease and polling is unchanged OMP-417-s05: after the worker_id advisory lock is held, a config whose capabilities (or, when capabilities is absent, whose handler keys) include omp.orchestrator also holds pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended('omp_jobs.controller:' || workspace_id, 0)) on that same connection for the process lifetime; if the try returns false the connection is closed and the process exits 3, including when the second process has a different worker_id.

trial_execution projects trial state from its latest root native job in omp_jobs into queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled; gating requires status succeeded, all trial jobs terminal (unsettled_jobs), and root settlement containing trusted audit and release receipts from issuers in the campaign compatibility manifest (missing_audit_receipt, missing_release_receipt, untrusted_receipt, issuer_not_in_manifest), adhering to R02 scientific success constraints

OMP-590-s04/OMP-605-s03-s01-s02: run_research_campaign consumes a loaded CampaignDefinition, prepares and admits a fresh campaign, transitions it to running, and proposes cached-digest evaluate trials. One run-specific capacity-one research.trial worker dispatches cpu-one jobs with 60-second leases and ticks only each target job. After each tick it reads the trial back from GET research and routes scoring and per-trial metrics strictly through read_trial_completion(client, store, key, campaign_id, trial, actor_id, definition.criteria[0].metric), so metrics and execution status come only from the verified evaluator receipt; observation payload metrics are never read and a missing trial, unsettled job, unbound or unverified receipt, or untrusted observation raises without conclusion. Transitions running to evaluating and concludes supported only when all trial criteria pass, returning campaign identity, outcome, reason, and trial metrics.

dispatch_trial enqueues the trial:<trial_id> native compute job with the research.trial capability on the work's proposed trial. factory builds the handler from worker options (harness_dir, work_url, bearer_file, workspace_id, default_timeout) and either calls an injected execute or constructs a WorkClient. run reads the trial and its campaign spec, resolves the trial's evaluator component descriptor, and loads the harness from harness_dir/<evaluator artifact_sha256>; a missing file or a bytes_sha256 mismatch fails the job with no observation and no run. The harness runs as a bash autoresearch.sh in a fresh temporary cwd with timeout campaign spec.resource_vector.max_wall_seconds else the default 600s, and its output is scanned for finite METRIC name=value lines, skipping __proto__, constructor, and prototype. The run is recorded through the WorkService as a legacy_autoresearch observation with observation_id uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, omp-job:<job_id>), source_ref job:<job_id>, the trial's campaign_id and trial_id, execution_status completed, crashed, or timed_out, payload {metrics, exit_code, duration_seconds, harness_sha256}, payload_sha256 v1.canonical.sha256 of that payload, and observed_at now. The job is settled succeeded only when the harness exits 0 within the timeout, with an evaluator receipt carrying the trial evaluator issuer, content_digest equal to payload_sha256 and trust verified; observe rebuilds the same settlement from the stored observation without running and run reuses it when one exists. python -m omp_work.jobs.research_trial check dispatches the job, ticks one worker, and prints {capability: autoresearch, passed, observation, receipt}

OMP-315-s01: local research runner on the egress worker jail. RunRequest(argv, workdir, ro_files=(), env={}, timeout=None, requires=(), capabilities={cpu}) rejects any env name other than PATH, LANG, TERM, TZ with ValueError('env_not_allowed'). RunResult has status completed|crashed|timed_out|canceled, exit_code, output of at most 1 MiB, duration, manifest, and manifest_sha256 (canonical sha256). Backend and RemoteRunner are protocols with name, capabilities, and run(request, cancel: Event|None). LocalJailBackend is local-jail.v1 with capabilities {cpu}: it calls run_sandboxed(root=worker, worktree=workdir, ro_binds=ro_files, env) with a MemoryRecorder and the jail cwd /work. BackendIncompatible(code) is raised before any process: a capability other than cpu (gpu, instrument) or resolve_backend('remote') is backend_incompatible; a requires name that is not an executable in /usr/bin or /bin is missing_dependency:<name>. The manifest is {backend, kernel, machine, executables {name: sha256 of the jail executable or requires tool}}. check_environment(m) returns differing keys in order backend, kernel, machine, then executables:<name>.

Effort gate at admission of policy-routed stage jobs: admit_stage_job(store, *, effort, effort_reason, **enqueue) validates the effort/reason pair with economy_effort.validate_effort first, so a failed pair raises JobError invalid_effort with the message as its single diagnostic before any store access or enqueue; on success it returns enqueue_job(store, **enqueue) from omp_work.jobs.admission, passing the remaining keyword arguments through unchanged. Not exported from jobs/__init__.py

NativeJobStore over role omp_work_app with RLS context. run_operation replays the same operation_id and request only inside its workspace and raises idempotency_conflict for another workspace or a changed request. run_operation binds the caller's workspace id into the request hash when the body does not already carry that id, and loads the stored result only in a query that also filters workspace_id. append_event writes only a native job in the caller's workspace. job_view/worker_view expose every row column. cancelled_ancestor walks to the nearest cancelled ancestor and raises invalid_request if a parent is outside the workspace. register_worker and drain_worker hash workspace_id into the request; capabilities are sorted and confined to the registered R02 worker descriptor; identical re-register replays; a changed or draining worker is job_worker_unavailable; drain is permanent. project_trial maps backlog=queued, admitted=leased, sealed=succeeded, failed, cancelled, and reports a job-less trial (or an unmigrated jobs ledger) as queued and ineligible; a trial is eligible only when every native job is sealed with settlement and settled_at. record_usage writes omp_jobs.usage_events and research_ledger.append_ledger_event once per operation. Optional internal absolute monotonic transaction deadline bounds nonblocking connection establishment, identity setup, SQL/advisory waits, commit acknowledgement and rollback; reserves min(250ms, one quarter of remaining allowance) for supported libpq cancellation and disposal without retry or background writer. Bounded connection establishment requires numeric hosts or Unix sockets; bounded mode requires libpq >=17; ordinary callers retain existing transaction and RLS setup. Expiry rejects further SQL and lost COMMIT acknowledgement reports outcome_uncertain rather than definite rollback. Optional internal TransactionDeadline control starts inactive and arms once with finite absolute monotonic time while the cursor is open; pre-arm admission/upstream work consumes no budget. The same nonblocking wait/cancel/disposal path bounds subsequent SQL and COMMIT/ROLLBACK cleanup, while an unarmed control preserves commit/rollback behavior. Supplying both deadline APIs or rearming refuses rather than extending the budget; unsupported bounded mode fails before entering the transaction.

record_usage runs through NativeJobStore.run_operation for WP5 accounting on omp_jobs.usage_events. Computes a stable usage_id from sha256(workspace_id, work_id, job_id, request_id). If job_id is provided, validates that the job exists in the workspace and matches work_id (job-less usage is permitted for preflight). An identical existing usage_id replays without writing or advancing step_index; any field discrepancy raises idempotency_conflict. A new row sets conversation_id to job_id or work_id, source_file to omp_jobs:native, step_index to 1 + max for that conversation/source_file, tokens to the sum of input/output/cache tokens only if all counts are known else NULL, and in the same transaction writes an outbox row with kind usage_ledger, CloseoutRecord committed state, revision 1, and the job_usage ledger event payload. OMP-404 appends to the same transaction one check_item_budget over the usage job's root_work_id (else the usage work_id): an item with no intake_publication budget writes nothing, a replay adds nothing, and each reached threshold writes its budget_alert outbox row; orch-worker-20261011-s01-s01: record_usage accepts an optional caller cursor and reuses validation, operation/usage idempotency, usage outbox delivery and item budget checks without opening or committing a transaction; omitted cursor retains the existing transaction path.; omitted cursor retains the existing transaction path. Shared validate_usage_counts enforces measured/estimated/unknown and nonnegative integer-or-None counts at both admission and record_usage boundaries; unhashable measurements map to invalid_request, unknown requires all counts None, and partial measured/estimated counts remain valid.

OMP-475-s04: WorkerConfig and JobWorker docstrings clarify capacity is an admission resource-weight budget rather than a concurrency setting, with tick running serially; OMP-400-s02: Native jobs runtime implementing Settlement(outcome, receipts, usage), Handler protocol (observe, run), load_handler factory loader, WorkerConfig, and JobWorker loop. start() enforces zero pending/drift on jobs migrations and checks migrations before register_worker; tick() runs reconcile_jobs, claim_job with resource_limits, observe() if lease_expired event exists, background renewal thread (interval lease_seconds/3) during observe() and run(), records usage, settles job with receipts and fence, and delivers outbox if ledger_path is configured; run_forever() runs tick() until stop_event is set OMP-417-s05: observe also runs when a lease_resumed event exists. Frozen raised from observe or run leaves the job leased and unsettled (status, worker, fence, and reservation unchanged) and tick returns that job_id; Frozen from run still joins the renewal thread before returning, and a renewal failure still returns the job_id without settling.; OMP-315-s02: cancel_requested event initialized on JobWorker and reset per claimed job before handler.observe or handler.run, renewal failure sets cancel_requested alongside renewal_failed and returns the job id unsettled OMP-590-s02: tick accepts optional job_id and passes it to claim_job. Renewal, observe or run, usage, settlement, and outbox delivery stay on that same path for the claimed job. With no job_id, tick still claims the oldest matching job. OMP-595-s03: JobWorker.tick initializes per-claim authority/cancellation before observe, renews throughout both observe recovery execution and run, and stops/joins renewal on every exit. Classifies agent_stop_engaged through shared current_authority query: frozen ownership signals distinct frozen-stop reason, lost ownership signals existing cancel_requested event even during stop, and released live authority continues renewal. Query failures and other renewal failures cancel and forbid settlement. Next tick starts uncancelled without reusing prior events. current_authority method delegates to lease query.; tick() runs reconcile_jobs, claim_job with resource_limits, observe() if lease_expired event exists, background renewal thread (interval lease_seconds/3) during run(), records usage, settles job with receipts and fence, and delivers outbox if ledger_path is configured; OMP-315-s02: cancel_requested event initialized on JobWorker and reset per claimed job before handler.run, renewal failure sets cancel_requested alongside renewal_failed and returns the job id unsettled OMP-590-s02: tick accepts optional job_id and passes it to claim_job. Renewal, observe or run, usage, settlement, and outbox delivery stay on that same path for the claimed job. With no job_id, tick still claims the oldest matching job.

OMP-404-s03: admit_mission_budget validates mission budget_policy as ItemBudget or returns held admission with an OMP-414 decision record; mission_intake_draft sets draft budget or returns None when held; OMP-430-s01: admit_mission_budget accepts standing_budget and admits it when budget_policy is absent

OMP-415-s03: derive_mission_events reads applied domain events and returns mission events, with no I/O. set_mission_status uses the last payload.mission.transitions entry: approved to running is mission.started with trigger status:approved->running; blocked, completed, or failed is mission.<status> with trigger status:<status>; abandoned emits nothing; any other target is mission.progressed with trigger stage_change. complete_work emits mission.progressed operation_completed when mission_for_work(aggregate_id, sequence) returns a mission UUID, and nothing when it returns None. create_decision emits decision.required decision_created only when payload.decision.mission_id is a UUID string, citing the decision id and each evidence_refs string. link_mission_work emits budget.threshold_reached with trigger budget_usd>=<fraction> when the last link moves drawn usd from below budget_fraction (default 0.8) of mission.budget.usd to at or above it, and emits nothing when the mission has no budget. record_finding emits important_finding with trigger finding_severity>=<threshold> when severity ranks at or above finding_threshold (low < medium < high < critical, default high), citing the finding id and evidence_refs. mission_event_id is str(uuid5(uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, "work.omp.dev/v1/mission-events"), "{event_id}:{type}")). evidence_refs are the domain event, then a decision, finding, or work_item id when the rule has one, then each evidence string. Payload prose such as a log field is not copied. Any outcome other than applied is skipped.

OMP-426-s02: pure mission-intake rules reusing evaluate_bounded_intake, material_cases, and mission_scope. clarifying_questions returns the capped blocking questions of a bounded-intake draft. draft_from_intake builds a MissionDraft from the intake goal statement, each criterion's observable_outcome in order, and each constraint's statement, with every other field from the scope mapping, and raises ValueError when the scope carries objective, acceptance_criteria, or constraints. Route is a frozen kind/cases/mandate_id record. confirmation_route computes material cases between the approved envelope and the revision dump: no cases approves the mission; otherwise, when undecidable is absent and the mission scope (goals={objective}, the draft's repositories, capabilities, tier3 classes, and budget usd ceiling against the standing ceiling) is approved, it is a standing mandate naming its mandate_id; anything else is an owner decision; OMP-417-s07-s04-s02: extracts scope_draft(draft: MissionDraft) -> MissionScopeDraft from confirmation_route's inline build. OMP-523-s05: clarifying_questions takes an optional selection (current|typed); omitted stays current, typed uses evaluate_typed_bounded_intake.

OMP-413-s03: pure D29 mission-scope rules. MISSION_STATUSES and TERMINAL_STATUSES; transition_allowed over ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, with every non-terminal status able to go to abandoned; material_cases returns sorted codes a-f, new when nothing is approved, or undecidable for a missing key or wrong type; outside_envelope is true for new, c, or undecidable

Single-process FastAPI model proxy CLI loads loopback-only bind, OperationsConfig, an automation execution capability, Gemini/Ollama transport routes and bounded request/response/time limits. Memory-only expiring grants pin implement routes selected by packaged routing policy and live admitted/queued call counts; control-only registration checks workspace, native job work/worker/fence/live lease, expiry and shared budget-derived USD ceilings. Native model bearers cannot register or revoke; route/options/size/authority/capacity refusals poison grants. Shared s01 admission and s02 transport account measured or estimated incurred spend before success; fresh stop/lease/expiry/revocation checks suppress output after in-flight stop. Control revocation waits for settlement and reports refused state and durable spend, including charged failures. Provider/control/model secrets cannot appear in responses; CLI access/error logging is disabled and restarts discard model tokens. Missing upstream results raise AssertionError even under optimized Python and map to proxy_refused without releasing output. The worker-native Gemini call is accepted at both /models/{id}:streamGenerateContent and /v1beta/models/{id}:streamGenerateContent with an empty query or alt=sse, so google.ts and the version-less worker baseUrl both route; any other path or query is refused route_mismatch before upstream. The native credential is the Bearer authorization when present, else x-goog-api-key; missing or unknown is 401, while control() stays Bearer-only. The charge-then-refuse path coerces the durable receipt sum through Decimal(str(...)), so a driver that returns a bare numeric cannot raise TypeError and become proxy_refused. Registration converts published item USD strings to Decimal before computing unused room, so budgeted orchestrator workers can receive grants. ProxyConfig.load validates mode 0600 and current uid ownership for the control capability file and calls read_secret for each configured transport key file, raising ValueError on unsafe permissions. Registration bounds grant expiry by shared task_deadline using persisted mission submitted-step controls and item budgets, or the 3600s fallback, rather than renewable lease expiry; live worker/fence/work authority remains required.; OMP-615-s02: validate immutable finite nonnegative premium reserves, load JSON tuples and Decimal allocations with asdict round-trip support, and refuse configured premium models before granting unless allocation is positive and model explicitly reserved; preserve dollar-budget enforcement; OMP-615-s03: ProxyConfig adds an overflow mode defaulting to alternate (compatibility) and accepting queue. Alternate validates both the primary implement route and its recorded alternate and refuses a missing overflow transport; queue validates and selects only the primary implement route. Queue registration ignores live in-flight counts, and invoke waits on a Condition over the registry lock for provider and total capacity bounded by the call deadline, refusing provider_saturated on timeout. The slot count is incremented atomically under that condition and decremented with notify_all in finally. Premium refusal, lease/budget admission and the alternate's immediate provider_saturated remain.

Model-call admission owns native-store transactions and RLS claims, serializes process-wide accounting with one lifecycle owner token, and acquires captured identity locks in receipt/project/mission/budget/root/task/job order. Admission revalidates stop state and native job lease/fence/work/root identity immediately after lock acquisition before authorizing spend with a fresh clock and enforcing project, item and task caps before sends. Completed deterministic receipts replay after cancellation or stop and immutable fingerprints reject changed intent. When stages.decide refuses qualification it records that decision, whose operation id is the decision id, and enqueues no job and creates no mission; otherwise owner.json permits mission submit/approve/start preparation and project_missions insertion; without owner.json confirmation remains with intake stages. Initial job enqueue and full submitted request/work identity publish atomically. A step job is orch:<mission_id>:<i>, kind compute, capability omp.orchestrator, resources cpu 1, memory_mib 256, gpu 0, model_calls 0. The stage of step i is the previous step's next_stage, and step 0 is intake. register_stage_operation(stage, run) binds run(StageContext)->Outcome. StageContext carries mission_id, workspace_id, project_id, work_id, step_index, stage, attempt, repair_round, request, prior outcomes by stage, lease, lease_ok, intents, service, the automation principal, projects, and config. command(type, payload) calls WorkService.execute with envelope ids uuid5 of the mission, the step, the type, and the call ordinal, so a re-run replays. act(operation, resolved, executor, rule_id) runs only the executor recovery when an intent is already open; otherwise it records action_allowed or action_refused around control_actions.perform, with decision_id the answered decision for that rule and hold the stage payload. command and act both check the stop first and raise jobs.worker.Frozen. Outcome carries outcome (succeeded, failed, crashed, or waiting), data, action, new_scope, budget_exhausted, blocker, and verdict. Facts are the stop, the mission status, qualification.qualified, the outcome and prior, the item-budget ceiling, attempts and repair rounds in the step log, whether other missions' leased orchestrator jobs are under qualification.max_workers, the routing-policy alternate, and an unprocessed terminal_request. A confirm decision of d23-owner-confirm before the operation has run is rewritten to a dispatch, the stage runs, and the recorded outcome is decided again. Apply records every step before its effect. advance, retry, repair, reroute, and reschedule enqueue the next step job. pause records the decision (an existing one counts as recorded), sets the mission paused with cause policy_rule and that rule id, and enqueues one wait job. The wait job polls every wait_seconds inside its lease, records nothing while the decision is unanswered, re-enqueues itself, and on an answer sets the mission running or applies the answer. abandon acts mission_abandon and then sets the mission abandoned with cause decision. redefine acts scope_broaden and then revise_mission with the draft carried by the terminal request. observe settles from a recorded outcome; when the stage has not finished it records a recovery step with rule lease-recovery and re-runs. dry_run returns the decision and writes nothing. qualify(lock_map, out) runs each mapped pytest with this interpreter and writes {release, results: {key: {item, test, result}}}. factory(config_path) returns the OrchestratorHandler for the jobs worker and accepts an operations or ops dict. The CLI serves submit, status, request-terminal, dry-run, and qualify, with --config on each command that loads orchestrator.json.
